facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley first referred three toothless snout fragments from the Lower Cretaceous Cambridge Greensand of England to the genus Ornithocheirus in 1869.
facts.quote: In 1869, Harry Govier Seeley, cataloguing the fossils of the Sedgwick Museum at Cambridge, referred three snout fragments of toothless pterosaur specimens from the Lower Cretaceous Albian Cambridge Greensand of England to Ornithocheirus simus.

facts.statement: Seeley provisionally named the fragments a separate genus called Ornithostoma, derived from Greek words for "bird" and "mouth".
facts.quote: Therefore, he provisionally named them as a separate genus Ornithostoma, the name derived from Greek ὄρνις, ornis, "bird", and στόμα, stoma, "mouth".

facts.statement: In 1891, Seeley formally named the type species Ornithostoma sedgwicki and referred pelvis elements to it, claiming they were identical to Pteranodon.
facts.quote: In 1891 however, he named the type species Ornithostoma sedgwicki Seeley 1891, apart from the snout fragments also referring to pelvis elements, claiming it was identical to Pteranodon and had priority.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ornithostoma is a snout fragment approximately five centimeters long.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is a snout fragment with a length of about five centimetres or two inches.

facts.statement: The known fossils of Ornithostoma show toothless jaws with low protruding rims and lack a crest.
facts.quote: There is no crest and the jaws are toothless but featuring low protruding rims.

facts.statement: In 1914, Reginald Walter Hooley incorrectly referred additional specimens, including a skull fragment with a crest base and postcranial fragments, to Ornithostoma.
facts.quote: In 1914, Reginald Walter Hooley reviewed the material. He, incorrectly, claimed the pelvis elements were misidentified parts of the notarium of the shoulder girdle and referred several additional specimens to Ornithostoma, among them a skull fragment featuring a crest base, specimen CAMSM B.54406, and postcranial fragments such as vertebrae and limbs.

facts.statement: S. Christopher Bennett considered Ornithostoma distinct from Pteranodon due to jaw ridges but concluded it was a nomen dubium in 1994.
facts.quote: In a 1994 paper, S. Christopher Bennett like Lydekker considered Ornithostoma to be distinct from Pteranodon, mainly because of the lower edge ridges of the jaw. He also concluded that it was a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: David Unwin rejected the nomen dubium status in 2001, arguing Ornithostoma is a valid genus in Pteranodontidae with a wingspan of 2-3 meters based on limited material.
facts.quote: This in 2001 was rejected however, by David Unwin who thought Ornithostoma to be a valid genus belonging to the Pteranodontidae, but limited the referable material to the original three fragments, including perhaps CAMSM B.54406, and places the wingspan of Ornithostoma at 2-3 meters.

facts.statement: In 2012, Alexander O. Averianov suggested Ornithostoma belongs to Azhdarchoidea based on a combination of jaw and postcranial traits.
facts.quote: In 2012, Alexander O. Averianov again recombined the holotype with CAMSM B.54406 and selected postcrania, the combination showing traits that indicated a position in the Azhdarchoidea, representing an animal similar in some ways to Tapejara.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies suggest Ornithostoma is a member of the family Chaoyangopteridae.
facts.quote: Subsequent studies suggest Ornithostoma is a member of Chaoyangopteridae.

facts.statement: The species formerly known as Ornithostoma orientalis was renamed Bogolubovia orientalis and transferred to the family Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: It has been renamed Bogolubovia orientalis (Nesov & Yarkov 1989) and been transferred from the Pteranodontidae to the Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: Ornithostoma is a genus created in 1871 by H. Govier Seeley for fragmented bone remains, mostly jaws, of a toothless pterosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of England.
facts.quote: Ornithostoma (nombre que significa "boca de ave") es un género creado en 1871 por H. Govier Seeley para un cierto número de restos óseos fragmentados, mayormente de mandíbulas, de un pterosaurio desdentado del Cretácico Superior de Cambridge Greensand en Inglaterra.

facts.statement: In 1994, S. Christopher Bennett noted that Ornithostoma has been treated as a wastebasket taxon for remains lacking distinctive features, similar to the dinosaur Megalosaurus.
facts.quote: En 1994 S. Christopher Bennett consideró a Ornithostoma distinto de Pteranodon. Infortunadamente Ornithostoma ha sido tratado como un taxón cajón de sastre, es decir, una conveniente etiqueta para restos que no tienen características distintivas, en forma similar al caso del dinosaurio Megalosaurus.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Ornithostoma as Azhdarchoidea.
The time range for Ornithostoma is estimated from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Ornithostoma is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur that lived in Europe during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 110 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Ornithostoma (meaning "bird mouth") is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period (Albian stage) of Europe, around 110 million years ago.
